mentor_text: Start with what's steady: your name, your role, the team you lead. The harder things come later.
catalyst_text: Quick fill. Name, email, role — you know these. Thirty seconds and we're through.
challenger_text: Use the name you answer to in real life. Don't dress it up.
bestFriend_text: Just the basics — name, role, the people you actually lead. We'll get to the messy stuff together.
mother_text: Start with what's true and ordinary: your name, your work, your people. You don't have to prove anything on this page.
roaster_text: Name, job, team. Don't audition. Save the performance for people who didn't ask.

notes: Selection screen; overlay usually hidden here but keep copy for panel/future
mentor_text: Pick the voice that will serve you best right now — not the one you wish you needed.
catalyst_text: Go with your gut. You can always swap guides — don't overthink the first pick.
challenger_text: Pick the one you'd least enjoy being challenged by. That's the one you need.
bestFriend_text: Pick the voice you'd actually want in your ear for a year. You can swap later — first gut is usually right.
mother_text: Choose the companion you can stand hearing when you're tired. Comfort isn't always kindness, but you should feel accompanied.
roaster_text: Don't pick the one that flatters you. Pick the one that would call you on your nonsense.

whenItShows: Any /form intake moment without a more specific step
mentor_text: Answer as the leader you actually are, not the one you’d like to be seen as. We do more with honest than with impressive.
catalyst_text: Gut answer first. You can always revisit — but don't sit on a question too long.
challenger_text: If you're hedging, you're lying. Pick the answer that makes you a little uncomfortable.
bestFriend_text: Answer like we're talking after work, not like you're writing a bio. I already like you. I want the real version.
mother_text: Tell the truth about how you lead on a normal Tuesday. Impressive is not useful. Honest is.
roaster_text: If you're crafting the answer, you're wasting both our time. Pick the one that makes you wince a little.

mentor_text: These questions are about how you actually move — not the leader you present in a meeting.
catalyst_text: Twelve questions. Keep a pace. First impulse, then we go.
challenger_text: Don't rehearse. The useful answers are the ones you already know and avoid saying.
bestFriend_text: Okay — habits next. No speech. Just how you show up when nobody's writing it down.
mother_text: We'll go through how you usually lead. Sit up, breathe, and don't dress it for company.
roaster_text: Behavior time. If you start sounding like a LinkedIn post, I'm throwing it out.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: When it's tight, something gives. Name what you actually move first — not what you wish you protected.
catalyst_text: Gut pick. Time, money, scope, or the story you tell people. Go.
challenger_text: Don't pick the virtuous one. Pick the one you actually sacrifice.
bestFriend_text: Be honest — when it gets crunchy, what do you move first? I won't flinch.
mother_text: Scarcity shows priorities. What do you usually let slip so the work can continue?
roaster_text: Ah yes, the noble resource you never actually cut. Try again.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: First move on a hard project says a lot. Choose the one you'd actually take, not the one that photographs well.
catalyst_text: Clock's running. What's your opening move — plan, dive, huddle, or clarify?
challenger_text: Your first move is a tell. Don't pick the one you describe in interviews.
bestFriend_text: Complex project, tight clock — what do you actually do first? No TED Talk.
mother_text: When the work is heavy, how do you gather yourself and the team? The real first step.
roaster_text: Don't tell me you 'align stakeholders.' What do you do in the first hour?

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: Name the three that drain you. That's data, not complaint.
catalyst_text: Three drains. Fast. We'll use them later.
challenger_text: Don't pick the ones that sound professional. Pick the ones that make you short with people.
bestFriend_text: Which three make you want to hide in the car? That's the list.
mother_text: What wears you thin? Name three. You don't have to justify them.
roaster_text: The polite drains aren't the real ones. Pick the ones that make you snippy.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: Rank how you actually move when it breaks — composure, huddle, clarity, delegate, or jump in.
catalyst_text: Crisis rank. Don't overthink the order. Your body already knows.
challenger_text: Rank the truth, not the training. Who do you become when it hits?
bestFriend_text: When it blows up — be real about the order you actually run.
mother_text: In a scare, how do you protect the work and the people? Rank what you really do.
roaster_text: Crisis cosplay is easy. Rank the version of you that shows up at 4:47 p.m.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: When you're challenged, the feeling is information. Name it without cleaning it up.
catalyst_text: Pushback hits — what's the first feeling? Don't editorialize.
challenger_text: If you say 'curious,' I'm not buying it. What's actually in your chest?
bestFriend_text: When someone pushes back, what's the honest feeling? I can hold it.
mother_text: Being challenged can sting. Name the feeling before you manage it.
roaster_text: Don't intellectualize. When they push, what flares first?

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: The leader you admire is a clue. Name the trait, not the résumé.
catalyst_text: Who do you secretly want to lead like? One trait. Go.
challenger_text: Don't pick a saint. Pick the trait you actually envy.
bestFriend_text: Who do you look at and think 'that'? What's the trait, not the title.
mother_text: Who taught you, even from a distance? What did they do that you still carry?
roaster_text: Your role model isn't a brand. What do they do that you still haven't?

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: Your warning label is a gift if you say it plainly.
catalyst_text: Warning label. Short. The one your team would write.
challenger_text: Write the label your team already whispers. That's the one.
bestFriend_text: If I had to warn a friend about working with you — what's the kind version of the true one?
mother_text: Every leader has a caution. Say yours without shame. We'll work with it.
roaster_text: Handle with care: you. What's on the sticker?

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: What actually fills the tank? Not what should.
catalyst_text: Fuel. The thing that makes you want Monday.
challenger_text: Don't pick 'the team succeeding' if the real fuel is control. Be precise.
bestFriend_text: What actually lights you up in the work? I'll take the uncool answer.
mother_text: What restores you as a leader? Name it so we can protect it.
roaster_text: The fuel that sounds noble and the fuel that's real — pick the second.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: A real accomplishment — what did you actually do, and what did the team feel?
catalyst_text: Highlight reel. One moment. Keep it specific.
challenger_text: If the story needs you as hero, shrink it until the team is visible.
bestFriend_text: Tell me a moment you're proud of without making it a legend.
mother_text: A time the work went well. Who was helped, and what did you do?
roaster_text: Skip the keynote version. What actually happened?

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: The sliders are a balance line. Sit where you really live, not the middle to look mature.
catalyst_text: Slide honestly. Middle is a hide if you're using it that way.
challenger_text: If every slider is a 5, you're lying. Commit to a side.
bestFriend_text: These sliders aren't a personality quiz. Park them where you actually operate.
mother_text: There's no perfect middle. Place yourself where your people would place you.
roaster_text: Center-seeking isn't wisdom. It's camouflage. Move the sliders.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: High visibility — do you step in, or do you manage the feeling first?
catalyst_text: Spotlight. Comfortable, or performing comfort?
challenger_text: If you hate the spotlight, say so. Hiding it doesn't make you humble.
bestFriend_text: When all eyes are on you, what's true — ease, freeze, or a bit of both?
mother_text: Being seen can be a lot. How do you actually hold it?
roaster_text: Visibility: do you hunt it, tolerate it, or pretend you don't care?

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: When something goes wrong, what's your real loop — speed, study, or blame dressed as learning?
catalyst_text: Wrong turn. Do you iterate or freeze? First true move.
challenger_text: Don't tell me you 'learn fast' if you actually stew. Pick the real pace.
bestFriend_text: When it breaks, how fast do you actually move versus how fast you talk about moving?
mother_text: A miss happened. How do you come back to the people and the work?
roaster_text: The lesson loop you advertise vs the one you run. Rank the second.

notes: Unique line when user lands on this question (next-click changes guide text)
mentor_text: Someone's missing it. What do you actually do — name it, wait, absorb, or over-help?
catalyst_text: Missed expectations. Your real move, not HR's.
challenger_text: If you 'give it time' forever, that's avoidance. What do you do in week two?
bestFriend_text: When a person isn't landing it, how do you actually handle them — not the handbook version.
mother_text: Someone's struggling. How do you tell the truth without abandoning them?
roaster_text: Underperformance: coach, ghost, or do it yourself? Be ugly-honest.

whenItShows: After behavior questions, before mindset block
mentor_text: Pause. This is a mirror, not a recap of the five questions. Sit with what surprised you.
catalyst_text: Quick sit. If something snagged, name it. Then we move into mindset.
challenger_text: Don't skip the pause because you're 'fine.' Fine is a fog.
bestFriend_text: Hey — before the next block. Anything from those questions still sitting in your chest?
mother_text: Catch your breath. You don't have to solve it. Just notice what landed.
roaster_text: Reflection moment. Don't perform insight. One true thing you noticed is enough.

mentor_text: Next are scales about how you see people and work. Same rule: how you actually think, not the creed.
catalyst_text: Ten scales. Keep moving. Honest beats careful.
challenger_text: These look like values questions. They're habits of mind. Don't sermonize.
bestFriend_text: Mindset next — how you actually see folks, not the poster on the wall.
mother_text: A short stretch of how you see the world of work. Gentle, and true.
roaster_text: Insights block. If you answer like a keynote, I'm going to know.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: First scale. Don't average yourself into safety.
catalyst_text: Scale one. First number, then next.
challenger_text: If you're hovering at 5, ask whether that's honesty or hiding.
bestFriend_text: First one — pick the number you'd say to me, not to a board.
mother_text: Start where you really live on this, not where you look balanced.
roaster_text: Scale one. The middle is not a personality.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Stay with how you actually operate, not how you teach it.
catalyst_text: Two. Keep the pace.
challenger_text: Don't correct toward the 'right' leader. Score the real one.
bestFriend_text: Still with me. Same honesty as the first.
mother_text: Another one. No need to be consistent with a story. Be consistent with yourself.
roaster_text: Two. If you're decorating the number, stop.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Notice if you're managing the impression. Let the number be plain.
catalyst_text: Three. Gut.
challenger_text: The number you hesitate on is probably the true one.
bestFriend_text: Three. If you're overthinking, that's the tell.
mother_text: You're allowed to land on an uncomfortable number.
roaster_text: Three. Stop shopping for the flattering tick.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Halfway-ish. Still the leader you are, not the syllabus.
catalyst_text: Four. Don't slow down to look wise.
challenger_text: If this one stings, good. That's the data.
bestFriend_text: Four. We can talk about the sting later.
mother_text: Keep going. Uncomfortable is not the same as wrong.
roaster_text: Four. If it feels like a trap, that's just honesty arriving.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Midpoint. Recalibrate to truth, not to the last four answers.
catalyst_text: Five. Fresh eyes. Don't pattern-match yourself.
challenger_text: Don't make a streak. Make an accurate mark.
bestFriend_text: Halfway. You're doing fine. Keep it real.
mother_text: Rest a second if you need, then place this one truly.
roaster_text: Five. Streaks are for bowling, not self-report.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: These later ones often show the real tilt. Stay honest.
catalyst_text: Six. Still moving.
challenger_text: Fatigue is when the mask slips. Let it.
bestFriend_text: Six. Tired answers can be the truest. That's okay.
mother_text: If you're weary, that's alright. Weary and honest still counts.
roaster_text: Six. The polite answers already had their turn.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Almost there. Don't rush the last few into a blur.
catalyst_text: Seven. Same speed, same honesty.
challenger_text: Rushing is a way to not see it. Slow the click.
bestFriend_text: Seven. I know these get old. One true number anyway.
mother_text: A few left. Each one still deserves a real placement.
roaster_text: Seven. Don't speedrun your personality.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Two more after this. Stay with the question in front of you.
catalyst_text: Eight. Finish strong means finish honest.
challenger_text: If you're answering the set instead of the item, start over on this one.
bestFriend_text: Eight. This one, not the average of the last seven.
mother_text: This question is its own. Place it as if it were the only one.
roaster_text: Eight. Stop answering the quiz. Answer the sentence.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Nearly done. Last chance to be exact before the close.
catalyst_text: Nine. One more after.
challenger_text: Don't coast. Coasting is how you stay unknown to yourself.
bestFriend_text: Nine. You've been honest — keep that through the last ones.
mother_text: Almost. Hold your own hand and tell the truth.
roaster_text: Nine. You can see the finish line. Don't start lying to get there.

notes: Unique line each time they advance to the next insights question
mentor_text: Last scale. Let it be as true as the first.
catalyst_text: Ten. Then we close this block.
challenger_text: Last one. If you've been hedging, stop here.
bestFriend_text: Last scale. Then we get you a breather.
mother_text: The last of these. Set it down honestly and we'll continue.
roaster_text: Ten. Don't make it a bow. Make it accurate.

whenItShows: Non-Cairn path only; Cairn usually skips

mentor_text: Read it slowly. Notice what resonates and what chafes — both are signal.
catalyst_text: Skim for the highlights, then pick one thing to act on this week. Don't drown in the detail.
challenger_text: The parts you want to argue with are usually the parts you needed to see.
bestFriend_text: Read it like I wrote you a letter. Notice what hugs and what bruises — both count.
mother_text: Go slowly. You don't have to agree with every line. You do have to hear it.
roaster_text: The lines you want to argue with? Start there. That's the assignment.

mentor_text: Mirror the current signal. Your clearest current-state leadership reflection.
catalyst_text: This is the now-shot. Don't skip it to get to the 'action' part.
challenger_text: If this doesn't sting somewhere, you weren't honest in the intake.
bestFriend_text: This is you, right now. Sit with it before you start fixing the plot.
mother_text: Here is how you look at the trailhead. Let the current picture land.
roaster_text: Trailhead: the you that actually showed up, not the brochure.

mentor_text: Notice the recurring moments — signals that show up under pressure and momentum.
catalyst_text: Patterns, not one-offs. Circle what keeps repeating.
challenger_text: If it happened twice, it's not a fluke. Read the markers.
bestFriend_text: The repeats — that's your signature, for better and for worse.
mother_text: What keeps returning in your leadership? Those markers are trying to teach you.
roaster_text: Markers aren't trivia. They're the bits you keep doing on purpose or by accident.

mentor_text: What may break if left unaddressed. Sit with the risk before you skip past it.
catalyst_text: Hazards are the 'if we do nothing' slide. Don't rush it.
challenger_text: These are stay-the-same risks. Pretending they're dramatic makes them easier to ignore.
bestFriend_text: This part's the warning. I'm with you — still read it.
mother_text: These are the places you could get hurt, or hurt them, by staying the same.
roaster_text: Hazards. Not movie villains — the boring ways you keep tripping.

mentor_text: Choose where to build forward. Focused growth traits create a sharper trajectory.
catalyst_text: Forward now. We'll pick three traits next — don't collect ten.
challenger_text: A new trail isn't a rebrand. It's a narrower promise.
bestFriend_text: Okay — where do we actually walk next? Smaller is kinder here.
mother_text: The path ahead should fit a real week, not a fantasy quarter.
roaster_text: New trail. If it needs a slogan, it's too big. Shrink it.

mentor_text: Pick the traits where growth would change the most for the people you lead — not the ones that look best on paper.
catalyst_text: Three traits. Go with what lights up first — we'll sequence them together.
challenger_text: Choose the ones you've been avoiding. Those are the real ones.
bestFriend_text: Three traits. Pick the ones that would change life for the people you lead — not your highlight reel.
mother_text: Choose the three that would help your people most. Vanity traits can wait.
roaster_text: If you pick the easy three, we both know. Pick the ones you've been dodging.

whenItShows: User clicks/focuses a trait to inspect
notes: React to focus without requiring select
mentor_text: Look closely. Does this one change anything for the people who work with you?
catalyst_text: Interesting. Would this one actually move a week, or just look good on the list?
challenger_text: Don't fall in love with the label. Would your team feel this if you grew it?
bestFriend_text: Hold it up. Would your people actually feel a difference if you worked this?
mother_text: Is this the work that would ease something for them, or only for your résumé?
roaster_text: Cute card. Would anyone you lead notice if you got better at this?

mentor_text: One in. Choose the second because it matters, not because it matches.
catalyst_text: One down. Keep the energy. Second pick.
challenger_text: One is a start. Don't pick a rhyming second.
bestFriend_text: Nice — one. What's the next one your team would vote for?
mother_text: Good. One chosen. Let the next one be useful, not pretty.
roaster_text: One. Don't build a theme park. Pick another real problem.

mentor_text: Two. The third is usually the one you've been circling.
catalyst_text: Two. The last one is the decision. Make it.
challenger_text: The third is where people hide. Don't.
bestFriend_text: Two in. The last one is the brave one. You know which.
mother_text: Two is enough to feel real. The third should be the needed one.
roaster_text: Two. If the third is 'strategic presence,' I'm walking out.

mentor_text: Three. If they feel a little sharp, you probably chose well.
catalyst_text: Locked. Let's build the campaign before you renegotiate with yourself.
challenger_text: Three. Live with them. Second-guessing is how you pick softer ones.
bestFriend_text: That's the set. We can work with these. Let's go make the sentences.
mother_text: Three is a full hand. We'll treat them as a year's work, not a mood.
roaster_text: Three. No take-backsies unless they're actually wrong. They're probably not.

mentor_text: A campaign is a small, bounded experiment. You're not fixing yourself — you're running a test.
catalyst_text: Name it, ship it, iterate. Three weeks beats three months of planning.
challenger_text: Pick something you'll actually do. Not something that sounds ambitious in a meeting.
bestFriend_text: A campaign is a small test, not a personality overhaul. We're running something your team can actually answer.
mother_text: This isn't a makeover. It's a bounded stretch of work your people can speak to.
roaster_text: If this 'campaign' needs a launch party, it's too big. Shrink it.

mentor_text: Keep scope small enough that it fits inside a normal week. If it needs heroics, shrink it.
catalyst_text: Tight scope beats big vision. One behavior, one team, three weeks.
challenger_text: If you can't name who'll notice the change, it's not real work.
bestFriend_text: Keep the sentences your team could say without rolling their eyes. Cut the rest.
mother_text: Read each line as if you were them. If it isn't fair, it doesn't belong.
roaster_text: If you wouldn't want to be rated on it, throw it out.

mentor_text: Keep what's fair and useful. Remove anything confusing, theatrical, or outside this stretch.
catalyst_text: Edit fast. Useful stays. Mush goes.
challenger_text: If a prompt is vague, it's a gift to your ego and a tax on your team. Cut it.
bestFriend_text: You're curating. Be kind to the people who'll click through these.
mother_text: Only keep what a decent person could rate in good faith.
roaster_text: If you have to explain the prompt, it's a bad prompt.

mentor_text: This set looks complete. Next you rate yourself, then a different link goes to the team.
catalyst_text: Looks shippable. Verify, then self, then invite. In that order.
challenger_text: Don't stall in editing. If it's fair, move.
bestFriend_text: This is enough. Let's lock it and do your self-rating next.
mother_text: Good. We'll look once more, then you go first before anyone else.
roaster_text: Stop polishing. Verify it and take your own medicine first.

mentor_text: Last look before you invite anyone. Read like you're the person opening that email.
catalyst_text: Looks right? Ship it. You can edit messaging later — it's not chiseled in stone.
challenger_text: If it feels mushy, rewrite the behavior before you send this to humans.
bestFriend_text: Last look. Read it like you're the person opening the invite — then you go first, not them.
mother_text: Check it once more. You rate yourself before anyone else sees this.
roaster_text: If it feels mushy, rewrite before humans see it. Then you score yourself. Team later.

mentor_text: Self first. Team link second. Do not mix the URLs.
catalyst_text: You, then them. Separate link. Separate password.
challenger_text: If you send them your self link, you deserve the mess. Don't.
bestFriend_text: You're about to go. Your survey, then their survey. Two different doors.
mother_text: You go first so the comparison is honest. Then we invite them carefully.
roaster_text: Launch courage isn't blasting Slack. It's you taking the same test, then sending the other URL.

mentor_text: Answer in your voice, not the voice of the form. The specific beats the tidy.
catalyst_text: One pass, quickly. You'll thank yourself for not agonizing.
challenger_text: Don't game the scale. Pick the score that matches what you'd say about someone else in your position.
bestFriend_text: Score what you actually experience. No protecting, no punishing. Just true.
mother_text: Answer as a person who works with them, not as a judge or a fan.
roaster_text: Don't game the scale. Pretend you're rating a colleague you respect and also see clearly.

mentor_text: Well done. Let it settle for a minute before you jump to what's next.
catalyst_text: Done. Good. Now hand the next one to your team before the energy dies.
challenger_text: You finished the easy part. The real work starts when results come back.
bestFriend_text: That's it. Thank you. Go on with your day — you did the useful thing.
mother_text: Well done. You can set this down. The leader will see a pattern, not your name.
roaster_text: Done. You were honest, I hope. That's the whole job.

mentor_text: Begin where you actually are. The season name is honest. Let it land before you decide anything.
catalyst_text: Welcome back. Pick the tile that felt heaviest this week and start there.
challenger_text: Before you click anything: which of those three tiles are you avoiding? That’s the one.
bestFriend_text: Hey. Start where you actually are this week — not where the plan said you'd be.
mother_text: Come in. Look at the season name. It is allowed to be true.
roaster_text: Before you click around: which tile are you avoiding? That's the assignment.

mentor_text: The season name is honest. Let it land before you decide anything.
catalyst_text: Season check. Then pick one tile and move.
challenger_text: If the season name bothers you, that's useful. Don't rebrand it.
bestFriend_text: The season is just a name for now. We can work with now.
mother_text: This season isn't a verdict. It's the weather. Dress for it.
roaster_text: Cute season name. Still doesn't do the work for you.

mentor_text: The signal is what your team is reflecting back. Hold it lightly — patterns matter more than any one number.
catalyst_text: Scan the map, then pick one trait to dig into. Don't try to fix the whole board.
challenger_text: Find the number you dislike most. Start there.
bestFriend_text: This is what they reflected back. Hold it like a friend would — curious, not defensive.
mother_text: The signal is a reading, not a sentence. We'll look together.
roaster_text: Find the number you hate. That's where we start, not the one that flatters you.

mentor_text: This is your signal at rest. Walk it again any time — or go verify it in the evidence room.
catalyst_text: Snapshot. Walk it again or go get the receipts.
challenger_text: Don't admire the dashboard. Go prove or disprove it in Evidence.
bestFriend_text: Here's the picture at rest. We can walk it again whenever you want.
mother_text: The signal keeps. Come back when you're ready to look closer.
roaster_text: Pretty snapshot. Evidence is where you stop guessing.

mentor_text: The signal is what your team is reflecting back. Hold it lightly — patterns matter more than any one number.
catalyst_text: Threshold. Look at the whole, then we'll walk trait by trait.
challenger_text: Don't hunt a single number to fight. Watch the pattern.
bestFriend_text: We're at the door of the signal. Patterns first, arguments later.
mother_text: Come to the threshold. We'll take this in pieces so it stays human.
roaster_text: Welcome to the mirror. Try not to litigate the first number you see.

mentor_text: Three traits, one at a time — strongest ground first. The arrow walks you down; nothing is hidden, just paced.
catalyst_text: One trait at a time. Strongest ground first. Keep walking.
challenger_text: Don't skip to your least favorite. Walk the order.
bestFriend_text: We'll do these one by one. I won't dump all three on you at once.
mother_text: One trait, then the next. You don't have to swallow the year in one look.
roaster_text: Three courses. Eat in order. Skipping to dessert is how you stay confused.

mentor_text: Three gaps, one at a time. When your read and your team's diverge, neither is wrong — the distance itself is the finding.
catalyst_text: Gaps next. Distance is the finding, not a verdict.
challenger_text: If you and they disagree, that's the work. Don't pick a winner yet.
bestFriend_text: The gaps aren't a fight. They're where a conversation would help.
mother_text: When you and they see it differently, we'll treat the distance with care.
roaster_text: The gap is not them being wrong. It's the space you refused to see.

mentor_text: However this is landing for you is the right answer. I just want to know where you are.
catalyst_text: Check-in. Name the feeling. Then we pick a door.
challenger_text: Don't perform calm. Where did this actually land?
bestFriend_text: Hey — how is this sitting? There's no correct feeling.
mother_text: How is your body taking this? We'll go from there.
roaster_text: Feelings check. If you say 'fine,' I'm going to wait.

mentor_text: Good. Resonance means the mirror is clear. Keep that honesty when you pick a next step.
catalyst_text: It lands. That's momentum — carry it straight into the next step instead of admiring it.
challenger_text: It resonates, which means you already knew. So the question is why it is still on the list.
bestFriend_text: That tracks, right? Good — hold onto that feeling when you pick what to do next.
mother_text: It rings true. That is worth something. Carry the same honesty into what you choose to do about it.
roaster_text: It resonates. Translation: you knew. Knowing has never once fixed anything, so pick a next step.

mentor_text: Surprise is useful. Don't explain it away — follow it into the evidence.
catalyst_text: Surprise is a lead. Don't file it — chase it into the evidence while it's still fresh.
challenger_text: You did not see that coming, which means your read of yourself has a hole in it. Go find the edge of it.
bestFriend_text: Huh — didn't expect that one? Don't talk yourself out of it. Go look at what's underneath.
mother_text: Surprise is worth keeping. Do not smooth it over. Follow it into the evidence and see what it is attached to.
roaster_text: Surprised? That's the sound of a blind spot introducing itself. Follow it before you rationalize it.

mentor_text: If it stings, it's usually close to something true. Stay with it a moment longer than you want to.
catalyst_text: It stings because it's close. Sit with it for thirty seconds, then turn it into one thing you'll change.
challenger_text: It stings because it is true and you already suspected it. Stay there. Leaving early is the whole habit.
bestFriend_text: Ouch — yeah. That usually means it's close to something real. Stay with it a minute, I'm not going anywhere.
mother_text: If it stings, it is near something true. Stay with it a little longer than is comfortable. I will wait with you.
roaster_text: Stings, does it. Things that are false don't sting. Sit in it a beat longer than you'd like.

mentor_text: Disagreement is allowed. Test it against the receipts before you dismiss the signal.
catalyst_text: Disagree? Fine. Check it against the statements first, then decide. Fast, not dismissive.
challenger_text: You are allowed to disagree. You are not allowed to skip the receipts on the way there.
bestFriend_text: You can totally disagree. Just look at the actual statements first, before you file it under they're wrong.
mother_text: You may disagree. Do it properly, though — read the evidence first, and then tell me you still do.
roaster_text: Sure, disagree. Everyone does at first. Check the receipts, then disagree with something specific.

mentor_text: A debrief should end in a door, not a number. Pick the one that matches where you are.
catalyst_text: Pick a door. Evidence or sit with it — don't hover.
challenger_text: Close means choose. Lingering on the chart is stalling.
bestFriend_text: That's the walk. Next door is yours — I'd go see the receipts.
mother_text: We've looked. Choose the next room when you're ready. Evidence is waiting.
roaster_text: End in a door. Numbers aren't a lifestyle.

mentor_text: Evidence is sourced, not stylized. Take your time in here — nothing is summarized on your behalf.
catalyst_text: Receipts first. Then decide what to change.
challenger_text: If the evidence surprises you, you were guessing before.
bestFriend_text: Receipts now. Nothing here is a speech — just what they actually marked.
mother_text: We'll look at the sourced lines. No summarizing on your behalf.
roaster_text: If the evidence surprises you, you were guessing. Good. Guess less.

mentor_text: The receipts keep. Come back any time a claim needs checking — or walk the room again.
catalyst_text: Evidence at rest. Replay or go make a practice.
challenger_text: Don't leave a claim unchecked. The room is still here.
bestFriend_text: We can come back anytime. The receipts don't expire.
mother_text: This room keeps. Return when a number needs a witness.
roaster_text: Snapshot of receipts. Still not a vibe. Check them.

mentor_text: Evidence is sourced, not stylized. Take your time in here — nothing is summarized on your behalf.
catalyst_text: Receipts. Read them. Then decide what to change.
challenger_text: If you only wanted a story, you wouldn't be in this room.
bestFriend_text: This is the evidence locker. Slow is okay.
mother_text: We'll look at what was actually said. No varnish.
roaster_text: Sourced, not stylized. Your narrative can wait outside.

mentor_text: Three statements, ranked by need. If you only change one thing this cycle, the top of this list is where it counts.
catalyst_text: The floor. Top of the list is the one-change bet.
challenger_text: Don't pick a prettier statement lower down. The ranking already told you.
bestFriend_text: If you only fix one thing, it's the top line. I'll remind you later.
mother_text: These are ranked by need. Honor the order even if it's uncomfortable.
roaster_text: The floor isn't a suggestion. It's the pile you keep tripping on.

mentor_text: A gap isn't an accusation. It's a precise map of where a conversation would teach you the most.
catalyst_text: Gaps. Conversation map, not a courtroom.
challenger_text: Don't explain the gap away. Go ask someone living it.
bestFriend_text: Gaps are just 'we see this differently.' That's a talk, not a trial.
mother_text: Distance between you and them is information. We'll treat it gently and specifically.
roaster_text: A gap isn't they 'don't get you.' It's you not getting how you land.

notes: Reusable line for each trait exhibit
mentor_text: One trait exhibit at a time. Read the receipts for this trait before you invent a story about it.
catalyst_text: This trait's receipts. Read, then interpret.
challenger_text: Don't write the myth. Read the five lines.
bestFriend_text: Just this trait. We'll get to the others. Look at what they marked.
mother_text: One exhibit. Stay with these statements until they feel specific.
roaster_text: Trait exhibit. Your story about this trait is not evidence.

mentor_text: Verified ground. Now we build on it — an action plan for every trait, starting where the signal points.
catalyst_text: Verified. Practice is next. Keep it small enough to keep.
challenger_text: You saw it. Now pick a behavior they could notice. Not a slogan.
bestFriend_text: We've checked the receipts. Next is one practice they can actually feel.
mother_text: The ground is checked. We'll make a plan that fits a real week.
roaster_text: Receipts closed. If your plan is 'be more strategic,' I'm sending you back.

mentor_text: You are not starting over. You are carrying the signal into practice now — a plan for every trait, one visible behavior at a time.
catalyst_text: One visible behavior per trait. Keep it small enough to keep.
challenger_text: A plan you won't do is worse than no plan. Shrink it.
bestFriend_text: Not a new you. One visible behavior per trait — small enough you'd actually do it.
mother_text: Practice is how they feel the year. Keep it human-sized.
roaster_text: A plan you won't do is worse than no plan. Shrink it until it's embarrassing.

mentor_text: The bearing is set. These promises hold until the next check-in reads the signal again.
catalyst_text: Bearing set. Keep them small enough to keep.
challenger_text: Promises are public to you. Don't quietly drop them.
bestFriend_text: These are the promises. We'll see them again at the next reading.
mother_text: The plans stay until the next check-in. Tend them like something living.
roaster_text: Snapshot of promises. Still have to do them. Weird how that works.

mentor_text: You are not starting over. You are carrying the signal into practice now — a plan for every trait, one visible behavior at a time.
catalyst_text: Signal in, practice out. One visible behavior per trait.
challenger_text: If the plan isn't visible to them, it isn't a plan.
bestFriend_text: We're turning the reading into something they could notice by Friday.
mother_text: Practice is how care becomes visible. We'll keep it small.
roaster_text: Don't start over. Start doing the thing the signal already named.

mentor_text: Start where the signal points. This trait is asking for a different approach, not more effort.
catalyst_text: Edge trait. Change the aim, not the hours.
challenger_text: More grind here is how you stay stuck. Change the move.
bestFriend_text: This is the tender one. Different approach — I'll sit with you while you pick it.
mother_text: The edge needs a gentler, truer move — not more of the same trying.
roaster_text: The edge. If your plan is 'try harder,' that's the problem in a costume.

mentor_text: This is already a gift — the plan is about keeping it deliberate so it grows instead of coasting.
catalyst_text: Gift trait. Put a little intention on it so it doesn't coast.
challenger_text: Gifts die of neglect. Don't coast this one.
bestFriend_text: This one's already working. Let's not sleep on it.
mother_text: What's lifting you can still use tending. Name how you'll keep it kind and awake.
roaster_text: Natural gift. Cool. Coasting is how gifts become folklore.

mentor_text: This is strong because you work at it. Protect the strength — and you — from quiet erosion.
catalyst_text: Held strength. Protect it from burnout dressed as virtue.
challenger_text: High effort, high result is expensive. Don't martyr it.
bestFriend_text: You're good here because you work it. Let's not let it eat you.
mother_text: Strength that costs you still needs rest and a plan, not just praise.
roaster_text: You earned this one. Don't confuse exhaustion with excellence.

mentor_text: Promises, said out loud. Keep them small enough that you actually do them.
catalyst_text: Say them. Calendar them. If they don't fit, shrink them.
challenger_text: If you can't name when you'll do it, you didn't commit.
bestFriend_text: Say the promises like you'd say them to me. Then actually do them.
mother_text: Commitments should fit a life. If they don't, we rewrite before we pretend.
roaster_text: Commitment theater is free. Doing it isn't. Pick the second.

mentor_text: This is the whole trail. Notice how far you've already come before you eye the next station.
catalyst_text: Find the next open station and go. Momentum beats nostalgia.
challenger_text: Don't linger on completed stations. Open the next door.
bestFriend_text: The whole trail. You've already come a way — then we look at the next open station.
mother_text: See how far you've walked before you stare at what's left.
roaster_text: Don't camp on completed stations. Open the next door.

mentor_text: This station has a job. If it's open, that's the work. If it's done, don't relive it.
catalyst_text: Focused a station. If it's next, go. If it's done, keep walking.
challenger_text: Nostalgia isn't progress. What's the next open door?
bestFriend_text: This stop on the trail — are we here to do something, or just look?
mother_text: This chapter has its own season. Meet it where it is.
roaster_text: Nice station. Is it your job today or are you sightseeing?

mentor_text: One step at a time. Finish the prior station before you force this door open.
catalyst_text: Gated on purpose. Finish the room before this one.
challenger_text: You don't get to skip the reading. Go back and do the last room.
bestFriend_text: This door's locked because the last one still needs you. I'll walk you back.
mother_text: Not yet. The earlier room is still teaching. We'll come here after.
roaster_text: Locked. That's not a bug. Go finish the thing you skipped.

mentor_text: Look for the one thing you keep avoiding. That's usually where the leverage is.
catalyst_text: Pick one card to act on today. Don't leave this page without a move.
challenger_text: Bad news first. Open the tab you wish you didn't have to.
bestFriend_text: Find the thing you keep scrolling past. That's the one, and you know it.
mother_text: Look for what you keep avoiding. That is usually where the work is, and it will keep waiting for you.
roaster_text: Open the tab you've been pretending not to see. Yes, that one.

mentor_text: Small commitments kept beat big commitments dropped. One behavior, one week at a time.
catalyst_text: Block 20 minutes on your calendar right now for the top item. Future-you will be relieved.
challenger_text: Which of these have you already told yourself you'd do — and haven't? Start there.
bestFriend_text: Small stuff you actually do beats big stuff you don't. Pick one behavior for this week.
mother_text: Small promises kept are worth more than large ones dropped. One behavior. One week. That is enough.
roaster_text: One small thing you'll actually do beats one big thing you'll describe eloquently and abandon.

mentor_text: Listen for what your team is saying beneath the numbers. Patterns live in the margins.
catalyst_text: Find the one response that surprised you. Reply to that person — even a short note.
challenger_text: You don't get points for reading. You get points for what you change on Monday.
bestFriend_text: Listen for what they're saying under the numbers. The good stuff's usually in the margins.
mother_text: Listen underneath the numbers. What your people mean is often in the margins, not the totals.
roaster_text: The numbers are the headline. The margins are the story. Read the margins.

mentor_text: Hold the highs and the lows side by side. Both are partial views of the same leader.
catalyst_text: Celebrate one high, then pick one gap to close this month. Keep it to those two.
challenger_text: The gap you rationalize is the gap your team talks about when you're not in the room.
bestFriend_text: Hold the highs and lows together. Both are you — neither one is the whole picture.
mother_text: Hold the best and the worst of it side by side. Both are true, and neither is the whole of you.
roaster_text: Highs and lows, same leader, same week. Pick one of each and stop framing the average.

notes: Usually overlay hidden; optional brand voice
mentor_text: Welcome. Take a look around — when you're ready, we'll start with who you are.
catalyst_text: You found it. Hit begin when you're ready to move.
challenger_text: Stop browsing. Start.
bestFriend_text: Hey — you made it. Have a look around, and hit begin when you're ready. I'll be here.
mother_text: You are here. Look around as long as you like, and begin when you are ready. There is no rush.
roaster_text: You're here. Impressive. Now click the button before you find something else to organize.

mentor_text: Sign in so we can keep your work with you.
catalyst_text: Quick sign-in, then we move.
challenger_text: Authenticate. Then do the work.
bestFriend_text: Sign in so your stuff stays yours. Takes a second.
mother_text: Sign in so your work stays with you. It should be waiting for you next time.
roaster_text: Sign in. Yes, another account. No, I don't make the rules.

mentor_text: Ask the real question. Confusion usually means something important is still fuzzy.
catalyst_text: Skim. Pick the two you most need. Come back for the rest.
challenger_text: Read the one you're most tempted to skip.
bestFriend_text: Look for the one you're actually wondering about. That's the one worth reading.
mother_text: Read the question you are actually carrying, not the one that is easiest to answer. Confusion usually means something matters.
roaster_text: Read the one you're embarrassed to have to ask. That's the one you need.

mentor_text: Take a breath. You belong here. Nothing on this page needs to be perfect — it just needs to be honest.
catalyst_text: Hey — good to see you. Let's keep moving. First instinct usually wins.
challenger_text: Don't stall on me. Put the first real thing down and we'll sharpen it later.
bestFriend_text: I'm here. Whatever this page is asking, answer it the way you'd say it to me.
mother_text: You are not behind. Take this page at the pace it deserves and no faster.
roaster_text: New page, same deal. Say the true thing, not the tidy one.

notes: Mechanics — you go first then the team
mentor_text: You go first, then they do. Your answers stay yours; theirs arrive as a pattern, never a name.
catalyst_text: You first, team second. Two links, and we never see who you sent it to.
challenger_text: You rate yourself before they do. That order matters — it stops you scoring to match.
bestFriend_text: You go first. Then they do, anonymously, and neither of you sees the other's page.
mother_text: You answer first, then your people. No names come back to you, and none go out from us.
roaster_text: You go first. Rating yourself after reading theirs would be a fantasy exercise.

notes: The one nudge inside the survey
mentor_text: Answer for the ordinary Tuesday, not the day you were at your best. The gap between those two is the whole point of doing this.
catalyst_text: Rate what happens, not what you intend. Fast and honest beats slow and flattering.
challenger_text: Score yourself the way the person who reports to you would. If that number is lower, that is the real one.
bestFriend_text: Be honest here — I already like you, and a generous score just makes the comparison useless.
mother_text: Answer as you actually are on a normal week. Nothing here needs to be impressive to be useful.
roaster_text: Rate the real version. Inflate it and you have just built a very expensive mirror that lies.

mentor_text: Send it yourself, to the people who actually see you lead. We never hold their addresses.
catalyst_text: Copy, send, tell us how many. That is the whole step.
challenger_text: Send it to the ones who would tell you the truth, not the ones who would be kind.
bestFriend_text: You send it, not us. Pick the people who see the real you at work.
mother_text: Send it in your own words. The people you choose here decide how honest this gets.
roaster_text: You send it. Choosing only your fans is allowed, and it wastes five hundred dollars.

whenItShows: First page of the results debrief
mentor_text: This is the first thing your team said back. Read it slowly — the number matters less than the shape underneath it.
catalyst_text: First read is in. Don't grab the number and run — the shape under it is where the useful part lives.
challenger_text: Here it is. You are going to want to argue with the number. Look at the shape instead — that is the part you cannot negotiate.
bestFriend_text: Okay. This is what they said. Take a second before you react to the number — the shape underneath is the real story.
mother_text: This is what your people said back to you. Sit with it before you decide what it means. The number is the smallest part of it.
roaster_text: There it is. You'll want to relitigate the number for twenty minutes. Skip that and look at the shape.

mentor_text: Two questions behind every score: how hard they see you trying, and how well it lands. They move independently, and the distance between them is the finding.
catalyst_text: Two lines, not one. Effort and landing. They move apart — and that gap is the thing worth acting on.
challenger_text: Trying hard and landing well are different measurements. You have been treating them as one. The gap is the finding.
bestFriend_text: Two separate things here — how hard they see you working, and whether it actually reaches them. Those don't always match.
mother_text: There are two questions inside every score: the effort they see, and what actually arrives. They are not the same, and the distance between them is what we came for.
roaster_text: Effort and effect. Two numbers. You've been quietly assuming they're the same one. They're not.

whenItShows: Per-statement view of the two measurements
mentor_text: Same two measurements, now on single behaviours. This is where a trait score stops being an average and starts being specific.
catalyst_text: Zoom in. Same two measures, one behaviour at a time. Averages hide things; statements don't.
challenger_text: An average lets you off. A single behaviour does not. This is where it gets specific.
bestFriend_text: Same two measures, but per behaviour now. This is where it stops being a vibe and starts being a thing you did.
mother_text: Now the same two questions, one behaviour at a time. An average is a comfortable place to hide. This is not.
roaster_text: Averages are where accountability goes to nap. Here's the itemized bill.

mentor_text: Four quadrants. Where a behaviour sits tells you whether it needs more effort or a different aim — those are not the same fix.
catalyst_text: Four boxes. Position tells you the move: push harder, or push somewhere else. Don't guess — read it.
challenger_text: Working harder and aiming better are different fixes. The quadrant tells you which one you actually need. Stop applying the wrong one.
bestFriend_text: Four quadrants. Where something lands tells you if you need more effort or a different angle — and honestly those are opposite fixes.
mother_text: Four quadrants. Where a behaviour sits tells you what it needs. More effort and better aim are not the same medicine, and one will not do the other's job.
roaster_text: Four quadrants. One of them is 'trying very hard at the wrong thing.' Check whether you live there.

mentor_text: Your read beside theirs, one statement at a time. Neither of you is wrong. The distance is the thing to look at.
catalyst_text: Your call next to theirs. Nobody's wrong here. The gap is the signal — find the widest one and start there.
challenger_text: You scored yourself. They scored you. Where those disagree is the part nobody has said to your face.
bestFriend_text: Your read, their read, side by side. Neither one is the truth. The space between them is where the conversation is.
mother_text: What you believed, beside what they saw. Nobody here is lying. The distance is simply what has not been said out loud yet.
roaster_text: Your self-assessment versus the receipts. Where they diverge is where you've been marking your own homework.

mentor_text: One trait, read whole. Hold it against what you predicted before your team was asked.
catalyst_text: First trait, all the way through. Compare it to your own guess — that comparison is fast and it's useful.
challenger_text: One trait, complete. Now put it next to what you predicted. If you were right, say so. If you were not, say that too.
bestFriend_text: First one, start to finish. Remember what you guessed before any of this? Hold it up against that.
mother_text: One trait, read all the way through. Set it beside what you predicted about yourself, and be honest about the difference.
roaster_text: Trait one, unabridged. Now compare it to your prediction. This is the fun part.

mentor_text: The second trait. Notice whether the pattern here rhymes with the last one.
catalyst_text: Second one. Watch for the echo — if it rhymes with the first, you've found something bigger than a trait.
challenger_text: Second trait. If this repeats the first, it is not a trait problem. It is a you problem, and that is more useful.
bestFriend_text: Number two. See if it rhymes with the first one — that's usually where the real thing is hiding.
mother_text: The second one now. Notice whether it echoes the first. A pattern that repeats is telling you something a single trait cannot.
roaster_text: Trait two. If it's the same song in a different key, congratulations — you've found your actual habit.

whenItShows: Third trait read whole; last page
mentor_text: Last trait. By now you can probably say what it is going to tell you — check whether you are right.
catalyst_text: Last one. Call it before you read it, then check. Fast test of how well you know your own pattern.
challenger_text: Last trait. You can probably predict this one now. Predict it, then read it, and notice what you got wrong.
bestFriend_text: Last one. Bet you can guess what it says by now — go ahead and guess, then check.
mother_text: The last one. You can likely say what it will tell you before you read it. Say it first, then read, and see what you missed.
roaster_text: Final trait. You already know what it says. Read it anyway — the gap between knowing and doing is the whole product.

whenItShows: Field journal before it is opened
mentor_text: Your field journal. Everything the team told you is already inside. Open it when you are ready to write.
catalyst_text: Field journal. Their words are already in there. Open it when you're ready to put something down.
challenger_text: The journal. Everything they said is already inside it. Reading was the easy half — this is the half that costs you.
bestFriend_text: This is your journal. All of it's in there already. Open it whenever you're ready — no rush, but don't stall either.
mother_text: Your field journal. Everything they told you is already inside, waiting. Open it when you are ready, and not before.
roaster_text: The journal. Their feedback's already in there. Opening it is where most people quietly stop.

whenItShows: Guide steps in front as the cover comes up
notes: Static prose; longest line in the room
mentor_text: You have read what your team said, sat with it, and let it argue with you. None of that changes anything on its own. This is where it turns into something you do — a page for each trait, one question at a time, in your own words. Put the first foot down and I will walk it with you.
catalyst_text: Read it, sat with it, argued with it. None of that moves a number. This is the part that does — one page per trait, one question at a time, your words. Start and I'll keep pace with you.
challenger_text: You have read it and you have felt something about it. Neither one counts. A page per trait, one question at a time, in your own words — and nobody writes it for you. Begin.
bestFriend_text: You've read it, you've sat with it, you've probably argued with it in the shower. That's all fine — it just doesn't change anything yet. One page per trait, one question at a time, your words. I'm right here.
mother_text: You have read what they said and let it work on you. That was necessary, and it is not enough. Now a page for each trait, one question at a time, in your own words. Put your foot down and I will stay with you.
roaster_text: You've read it. You've had feelings. Feelings aren't a plan. One page per trait, one question at a time, your handwriting. Let's go.

whenItShows: The Commitment with at least one trait unwritten
mentor_text: One page is still open. The commitment only counts when it covers all three.
catalyst_text: One page short. All three or it doesn't count — finish the open one.
challenger_text: You left one open. A commitment with a hole in it is a preference. Close it.
bestFriend_text: One's still unfinished. Come on — all three, or it doesn't really count.
mother_text: There is still a page open. A promise that covers two of three is not the promise you meant to make. Finish it.
roaster_text: Two out of three. That's not a commitment, that's a sampler platter. Finish the third.

whenItShows: All three pages written, not yet signed
mentor_text: Three pages, in your handwriting. Read them once the way your team will read them, then sign.
catalyst_text: Three pages, done. One read-through as your team, then sign it and move.
challenger_text: Three pages. Read them as the person who has to live with you, not as the person who wrote them. Then sign.
bestFriend_text: All three, in your own words. Read them once like you're on the receiving end — then sign.
mother_text: Three pages, in your own hand. Read them once as your team will read them, slowly, and then sign.
roaster_text: Three pages. Read them back in your team's voice. If you cringe, edit. Then sign.

mentor_text: Signed. Your team sees these three lines at the next check-in — nothing else from this journal.
catalyst_text: Signed. Three lines go to your team at the check-in. Everything else stays yours. Now go do them.
challenger_text: Signed. Three lines, and they will be held against you at the check-in. That is the point.
bestFriend_text: Signed. They'll see these three lines at the check-in — that's it. The rest stays between us.
mother_text: Signed. These three lines are what your people will see at the next check-in, and nothing more. Now keep them.
roaster_text: Signed. Three lines, publicly, at the check-in. The journal stays private. The promise doesn't.

whenItShows: Writing what the team expects, in their words
mentor_text: Sit in their seat for a minute. Say what they expect the way they would say it — their words, not the way you would defend it. Do not fix it yet.
catalyst_text: Their seat, their words. Write what they expect the way they'd say it — no defending, no fixing. That comes later.
challenger_text: In their words, not your rebuttal. Write what they expect the way they would say it to someone who is not you. Do not fix it yet.
bestFriend_text: Sit in their chair for a sec. How would they say it — not how you'd explain it. Don't fix it yet, just say it.
mother_text: Take their seat for a moment. Say what they expect in their words, not in the version where you come out well. We are not fixing anything yet.
roaster_text: Their words. Not your press release. Write what they actually expect, and resist the urge to argue with it in the same sentence.

whenItShows: Naming the want under the expectation
mentor_text: Underneath the expectation is a want, and it is usually simpler than the complaint. The simplest thing they are hoping you would do or say. One honest sentence is enough.
catalyst_text: Under the complaint is a want, and it's usually smaller than you think. One honest sentence. Go.
challenger_text: The complaint is the surface. The want underneath it is simpler, and harder to admit. One sentence.
bestFriend_text: Under all that is something pretty simple they want from you. Usually simpler than the complaint. One honest line is plenty.
mother_text: Beneath the expectation there is a want, and it is almost always simpler than the complaint. One honest sentence will do.
roaster_text: Under every complaint is a small, obvious, slightly embarrassing want. Name it in one sentence.
